page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-2 is an ARM64-based virtual machine instance belonging to the c4a server family. It is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores using the Arm Neoverse-V2 processor architecture, operating with 1 thread per core. The system features 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 80 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate a split performance profile. Single-threaded operations demonstrate notable efficiency, with gzip compression and bzip3 decompression single-threaded benchmarks scoring in the strong category at 32.27 GB/sec and 13.96 GB/sec respectively. However, multi-threaded and memory-intensive tasks show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is rated as weak at 3616.42, and the overall PassMark CPU score is poor at 2155.3. Memory bandwidth write operations for large blocks are weak at 21.88 GB/sec, though read-only large block bandwidth reaches an average tier of 56.53 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is also limited, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the poor range at 413.52.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4a-highcpu-2 offers a low-overhead entry point into ARM-based compute instances, trading off high multi-core throughput and memory capacity for dedicated physical cores. This resource profile is suited for lightweight, single-threaded processing tasks, basic web serving, and development or testing environments that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not demand large memory footprints or high multi-threaded performance.
